savings.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_12292 (EO 12292, 46 FR 13967-13968, read once in full): secs. 1-9 amend nine orders, sec. 10 revokes thirteen orders or parts of orders, sec. 11 makes the whole order effective as of 1981-02-15; there is no savings, continuation, transfer or exception provision, and none of the listed revocations is qualified. Own-residual check, reading EO 10249 in full: it prescribed how the State Department serves other agencies' requests for foreign data (definition, obtaining the data, a statement of types of data and standards, priorities). It conferred no right or benefit, transferred no function, property or funds, and created no duty beyond the Department's own procedure; the statement and standards it required are administrative papers. research_rationale: EO 10249 (signed June 4, 1951; 16 FR 5309), read in full from the held FR text, prescribes regulations on Foreign Service reporting functions under sec. 311 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946, with no term or sunset. EO 12292 (signed February 23, 1981; 46 FR 13967-13968), read in full, says its purpose is to conform existing orders to the Foreign Service Act of 1980, revokes this order in sec. 10(e) and in sec. 11 makes itself 'effective as of February 15, 1981'. The date of the end is therefore 1981-02-15, the stated effective date, not the signing date. (The dossier labels the provision 'Sec. 9.'; the printed text reads 'Sec. 10.') The dossier's clause list omitted the operative lead, so I added it, giving five scopes. The held OCR of sec. 4 is damaged; the page image was not inspected, so original_pages_confirmed is false. Earlier-end test: the OFR catalog hits (2) and the dossier chain show only EO 12292; there are no U.S. Code or eCFR hits for this order, and no amendment, supersession or earlier revocation was found.
